posts.cooked:
Having recently discovered this game due to a friend of mine bringing it over when we get together to play board games I just had to get my own copy and I'm loving it to death. That being said I have yet to lose to a villain, mostly due to some very cheap shennanigans on the part of incapacitated heroes.

 

For example my friends and I decided to take on Iron Legacy expecting a tough fight or to get wrecked at the worst. Instead we were basically immortal. Once Bunker went down we just used his incapacitated ability to cycle Mr Fixer's Grease Gun card into his hand every time it went into the trash. We were completely from all damage, every single turn. Bunker was way more useful dead then alive. In fact as soon as an incredibly powerful card is drawn Bunker should immediately try and get himself killed. It's true that he could have never drawn the card, but The Scholar has a very similar one and realy once the card is drawn and used once Iron Legacy lost the fight, we couldnt be hurt by the environment or him at all. We didnt need to do anything but just sit back and wait for our better cards to come while we ignored everything every turn

 

By far the most rdiculous example though is in a recent fight against The Chairman. his minions had us on the ropes, we were completely unprepared having never fought him before. we all wnet down at about the same time aside from Mr Fixer. Then we noticed something, Tempest's ability made everyone immune to one type of damage for an entire round and aside from about 3 entire cards in The Chairman's deck he can only deal melee damage. So 1 hp fixer just beat the Chairman down from about full health to dead while being completely immune to anything The Chairman could do. Bunker was there so once again we could have infinitely cycled the "completely invincible for a turn" card but we didnt even need to.

 

I guess the point I'm getting at is that most heroes have a draw a card and play a card power along with one insanely powerful ability. Has anyone had similar experiences? Im considering house ruling something along the lines of only being able to use each incapacitated ability once

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
An incapacitated hero doesn't play a card or use a power, so they are intentionally given extremely strong incap abilities, because that's all they're good for.  It's true that some of them are VERY potent, but this just acts as a balancing factor in the game.  If you haven't lost yet, just give it time.  Even the most potent incap abilities are only sometimes the correct solution for the problem at hand.

If you think the villains are too easy, try fighting the Chairman (arguably even harder than Iron Legacy), the Advanced Ennead (about triple as hard as the non-Advanced version, and a heck of a lot of fun), The Dreamer with five heroes, or Advanced Citizen Dawn with three.  Make sure that you're selecting heroes at least semi-randomly, rather than picking ones you know will be strong in the match (whether alive or dead).  Among the less-strong heroes are Expatriette, Bunker, Haka and situationally Unity or Absolute Zero (those last two are "break the game in half" heroes if played to greatest effect, but can be a bit fragile; the others, except perhaps Haka, are simply a bit on the weak side); if too many of your games feature Legacy, Wraith, Nightmist, Scholar, or Omnitron-X (let alone several of these), who are the likeliest candidates for "tier 1" heroes, then you're probably performing a bit above average in general, though any hero is particularly strong if played against a villain whose weaknesses match what they can do.  (Dead Tempest, for instance, is extremely strong against Iron Legacy in particular, since almost all of Tempest's damage is the same type...against Miss Information or Grand Warlord Voss, both of whom have two damage types on their own card and more on their minions, he's much less efficient.)

With experience, you'll see that the balance point is pretty close to where it ought to be.  Sometimes you get utterly destroyed by a seemingly weak villain, sometimes you faceroll the tough guys.  I doubt very much you'll stay undefeated for more than a dozen or so games.

Difficulty 2 for La Capitan is almost certainly a misprint; it's never been confirmed but anyone who has played her and Kismet can tell that the two ought to be switched.  (Not that Kismet can't be devastating with the potential for huge bonuses to damage on both sides, but still, she has enough dead plays and little enough hero scaling that she compares very well to Plague Rat or Akash'bhuta.  A difficulty-3 villain, excepting the also-mismeasured Gloomweaver, should be reliably dangerous, not just occasionally so.)

True but those cards are The Contract and Hired Gun, so you will almost certainly see them.

Matty is one of the easier "hard" villains, though; she's possible to "solve" without too much trouble.  2 points of DR will make you invincible against her unless she has the damage-boosting Cohort in play.  If Scholar rocks double Flesh to Iron with Alchemical Redirection and the other heroes just play fodder to keep those in play (the Alchemical needs to keep getting replayed, but Scholar himself has recycling tech to help that happen), the Birds can be safely ignored, up until the moment they power a Grace Under Fire or a giant Get Out of the Way with Mortal Form to Energy.  Plus of course Tachyon has lots of tech to use against her, and any hero with even one point of DR has a huge advantage.  Tempest can set his Subwave to "projectile" and get down Otherworldly Resilience, that makes him immune to all but the cohort-boosted damage, though he has to refrain from Squalling.  Overall, she is definitely less hard than Iron Legacy and the Chairman.
